amending_instruments_note: NOT a complete amendment history. Only resolutions actually verified this pass are listed; other amendments between 2005 and 2026 certainly exist and were not enumerated. See known_unresolved_discrepancies.
verification_methodology_note:
PRIMARY SOURCE: the official Arabic PDF of لائحة مؤسسات السوق المالية hosted on the Capital Market Authority's own regulations page and linked from it -- https://cma.org.sa/RulesRegulations/Regulations/Documents/the_Capital_Market_Institutions_Regulations-ar.pdf -- fetched directly this pass (HTTP 200, 111-page born-digital PDF, 1,257,193 bytes, Producer 'Microsoft Word LTSC', CreationDate 2026-01-08). The link was read out of cma.gov.sa/RulesRegulations/Regulations/Pages/default.aspx (cma.org.sa 301-redirects to cma.gov.sa; both are the Authority's own domains), whose catalogue entry for this instrument shows issue date 27-June-2005 and last update 07/01/2026 -- consistent with the PDF's own cover page. ARABIC GOVERNS throughout; the English edition was used ONLY to confirm the citation and the article count and NEVER to correct, reconstruct or influence one character of Arabic.

CITATION CHAIN, verified: the PDF's own cover page states the Regulations were issued by the Board of the Capital Market Authority under Resolution No. (1-83-2005) dated 21/5/1426H (28/6/2005G), pursuant to the Capital Market Law promulgated by Royal Decree No. M/30 dated 2/6/1424H, and are 'المعدلة بموجب قرار مجلس هيئة السوق المالية رقم 2-3-2026 وتاريخ 18/07/1447هـ الموافق 07/01/2026م'. The ORIGINAL resolution number is independently confirmed by a SECOND OFFICIAL source, the Umm Al-Qura official gazette (uqn.gov.sa/details?p=26605), which cites 'لائحة مؤسسات السوق المالية الصادرة بقرار المجلس رقم (1-83-2005) وتاريخ 21/5/1426هـ', and by the CMA English edition's cover ('Resolution Number 1-83-2005, Dated 21/05/1426H Corresponding to 28/06/2005G'). The AMENDING resolution number 2-3-2026 is corroborated by the secondary source qanoonsa.com (p/515504), 'هيئة السوق المالية: قرار رقم (٢-٣-٢٠٢٦) اعتماد تعديل لائحة مؤسسات السوق المالية'.

RENAME HISTORY, established rather than assumed: this instrument was NOT originally called لائحة مؤسسات السوق المالية. Resolution 1-83-2005 (21/5/1426H) issued it as «لائحة الأشخاص المرخص لهم» (Authorised Persons Regulations). CMA's own announcement CMA_N_2764 (cma.gov.sa/MediaCenter/NEWS/pages/CMA_N_2764.aspx, Arabic and English) records that the Board approved amendments to the Securities Business Regulations, the Authorised Persons Regulations and the Glossary, INCLUDING 'تعديل اسم «لائحة الأشخاص المرخص لهم» ليكون «لائحة مؤسسات السوق المالية»' / 'amending the name of "Authorised Persons Regulations" to be "Capital Market Institutions Regulations"', effective 15/3/1442H (1/11/2020G), with certain provisions effective 28/5/1443H (1/1/2022G). It is therefore the SAME instrument under the SAME founding resolution 1-83-2005, renamed in 2020 -- not a new or separate regulation, and not a merger of two instruments. CMA does not publish the number of the resolution that effected the rename; that number is recorded as UNKNOWN, not guessed (see known_unresolved_discrepancies).

ARTICLE COUNT: 99, verified independently three ways and NOT taken on trust from the commissioning brief. (1) The Arabic PDF's own table of contents runs المادة الأولى ... المادة التاسعة والتسعون. (2) The enacting text was segmented by matching each heading against an EXPECTED Arabic ordinal sequence 1..99, which yielded an unbroken 1..99 run with no gaps, no duplicates and no مكرر articles. (3) The CMA English edition's body runs Article 1 ... Article 99. A fourth, secondary check (qanoonsa.com p/515505) also lists exactly 99 article headings. The census figure of 99 is confirmed correct.

TEXT EXTRACTION -- why the usual tools are wrong here, and what was done instead. The PDF's embedded subset fonts use Arabic LIGATURE glyphs whose ToUnicode CMap correctly maps one glyph to two or three logical-order code points (lam+meem, lam+alef, ta+meem, meem+jeem, ... 30 distinct sequences were enumerated directly from the two /Type0 font CMaps). pdftotext and PyMuPDF expand the CMap and THEN reverse the right-to-left run, which flips the characters inside every expansion (المملكة comes out as اململكة, لائحة as الئحة); pypdf orders them correctly but silently DROPS some ligature glyphs and mis-splits words. Neither output is usable as verbatim legal text. Text was therefore extracted at GLYPH level with pdfminer.six: glyphs are read in visual order with each multi-character CMap expansion kept as an ATOMIC token, the token list (not the character list) is ordered right-to-left, and embedded left-to-right material is un-mirrored. No character is ever substituted, invented, transliterated or reconstructed, and no whole-word guess list is used anywhere.

Four further, individually diagnosed source-layer artefacts were handled, each by a rule derived from measurement over all 111 pages rather than by guessing: (a) Arabic justification stamps narrow kashida STUB glyphs on top of real letters -- every stub is at advance/font-size == 0.095 and lies wholly inside a wider glyph's advance, while the narrowest real glyph in the file is the tatweel at 0.116; stubs are dropped, which removes phantom letters (إشعار was leaking as إ سشعار). (b) Combining marks are drawn at the x-origin of their base, so x0 is rounded to 0.1pt and the base is ordered first, keeping بناءً and تُعَدّ intact. (c) Word emits a real space glyph at almost every word boundary; at 19 boundaries inside the article text it emits none, leaving only a gap -- measured across the document, intra-word gaps never exceed 0.8pt and genuine missing-space gaps start at 1.5pt, so a space is restored where the gap exceeds 1.0pt AND no kashida stub was removed between the two glyphs (kashida stretching opens artificial 2.0-7.6pt gaps). (d) Some list markers are drawn with the digit and its period on baselines 3.2pt apart while the body line pitch is ~24pt, so lines are grouped with a 5pt baseline tolerance.

INDEPENDENT TEXT CROSS-CHECK: all 99 article texts were compared, article by article, against an independent secondary rendering of the same instrument (qanoonsa.com/p/515505). On a normalised comparison (diacritics, Arabic-Indic digits, alef/ya/ta-marbuta variants and punctuation folded) the median agreement is 1.0000 and the mean 0.9902; 97 of 99 articles agree at >= 0.99 and 98 of 99 at >= 0.97. Article 99 scores low ONLY because the secondary source's block for it runs on into that site's own page furniture; its actual sentence is character-identical to this track's. Every residual divergence was inspected by hand and in EVERY case the secondary source is the defective one -- it carries the very ligature-transposition defect described above, uncorrected (المشورة -> الموشرة, لا يجوز -> ال يجوز, العمولات -> العملاوت), plus silent editorial normalisations. Not one divergence was resolved in favour of the secondary source, and not one character of this track's Arabic was altered to match it. There are ZERO places where this track splits a word that the secondary source keeps whole.

VERIFICATION TIER: TIER_2. The CITATION chain alone would justify TIER_1 -- it rests on two independent OFFICIAL sources (cma.gov.sa's own PDF and the Umm Al-Qura gazette). But the tier is governed by the weakest meaningfully-sized portion of the track, which is the 99 article TEXTS: those rest on ONE official source (the CMA Arabic PDF) plus a SECONDARY cross-check (qanoonsa.com). No second OFFICIAL full-text edition of the current Arabic consolidation was obtainable this pass -- laws.boe.gov.sa is hard-blocked to this client, and the Umm Al-Qura entries reachable this pass cover individual amending resolutions rather than the full consolidated 99-article text. One official source plus one secondary cross-check is exactly TIER_2, and the track is recorded as TIER_2.

AMENDMENTS: the ingested text is CMA's own CONSOLIDATED CURRENT text, in which every amendment up to and including Resolution 2-3-2026 (18/07/1447H = 07/01/2026G) is already incorporated. Unlike some other CMA instruments, THIS PDF CARRIES NO PER-ARTICLE AMENDMENT FOOTNOTES -- there is no marking anywhere in the document of which articles a given resolution touched. No article is therefore flagged معدلة: doing so would require inventing an attribution the source does not make. All 99 records carry legal_status_ar = اصلية in the sense used across this corpus for a consolidated current text without published per-article attribution, and this limitation is restated in known_unresolved_discrepancies. No pre-amendment wording is reconstructed for any article.

SOURCE TYPOGRAPHY RETAINED: CMA's text uses the standard Saudi legal-drafting تطويل between noon and zay so that نزاهة/نزاع cannot be misread (بنـزاهة، النـزاهة، نـزاع، النـزاع, in Articles 5, 6, 14, 51 and 65), and the letter-ordinal هـ for fifth-level items. Both are verbatim in the source and are deliberately PRESERVED rather than silently normalised away.

SCOPE: the 99 numbered articles only. The Regulations also carry 11 annexes (الملحق 3-1, 3-2, 5-1, 5-2, 5-3(أ), 5-3(ب), 5-4, 5-5, 5-6, 5-7, 6-1), which are tabular/form material and are NOT ingested as records in this track; they were positively identified and excluded from article bodies, so no annex text has leaked into any article.

known_unresolved_discrepancies.description: The same resolution is printed in two component orders. The PDF cover page, the CMA English edition and the Umm Al-Qura gazette all render the founding resolution as (1-83-2005) and, on the same cover, the amending resolution as (2-3-2026). CMA's own web catalogue and the commissioning census render the identical resolutions as 2005-83-1 and 2026-3-2. These are NOT different resolutions -- it is a bidirectional-display convention, confirmed by reading the cover page's glyph positions directly (the digit groups are laid out right-to-left while each group reads left-to-right). This track records the form printed on the instrument itself, 1-83-2005 and 2-3-2026, and states the alternative form explicitly so neither can be mistaken for a distinct decision. UNRESOLVED only in the sense that CMA publishes both orders without ever reconciling them.

The rename of «لائحة الأشخاص المرخص لهم» to «لائحة مؤسسات السوق المالية» is CONFIRMED, with its effective dates, by CMA's own announcement CMA_N_2764 (Arabic and English): effective 15/3/1442H = 1/11/2020G, certain provisions 28/5/1443H = 1/1/2022G. However neither the Arabic nor the English announcement states the NUMBER of the Board resolution that effected it, and it does not appear on the current PDF's cover page (which names only the founding resolution and the latest amending one). The number is therefore recorded as UNKNOWN and is NOT guessed. Anyone needing it should obtain the 1442H Umm Al-Qura publication of that resolution.

This instrument has been amended repeatedly since 2005, but CMA's published consolidated PDF carries NO footnote or marker identifying which articles any given resolution amended, added or repealed. Consequently no article in this track is flagged معدلة/مضافة/ملغاة and status_counts is 99 اصلية / 0 معدلة / 0 ملغاة / 0 مضافة. This records the ABSENCE of published per-article attribution -- it must NOT be read as a positive assertion that no article has ever been amended, which would be false. The text ingested is the consolidated text as amended through Resolution 2-3-2026.

The amendment chain between the 2005 issuance and the 2026 consolidation is only PARTIALLY established. Confirmed this pass: the 2020 rename (effective 15/3/1442H, CMA announcement CMA_N_2764); Resolution 1-101-2023 dated 8/4/1445H and Resolution 4-87-2024 dated 16/01/1446H (both cited by the Umm Al-Qura gazette entry at uqn.gov.sa/details?p=26605, which amends Article 77, and 4-87-2024 is additionally printed on the CMA English edition's cover); and the current Resolution 2-3-2026 dated 18/07/1447H (PDF cover). Other amending resolutions certainly exist across 2005-2026 and were NOT enumerated this pass. amending_instruments therefore lists only what was actually verified and is expressly NOT a complete history.

The CMA English edition (cma.gov.sa/en/.../CapitalMarketInstitutionsRegulations.pdf) is a DIFFERENT, EARLIER vintage: its cover states it is amended by Resolution 4-87-2024 dated 16/01/1446H, whereas the governing Arabic edition ingested here is amended by Resolution 2-3-2026 dated 18/07/1447H. The English was used ONLY to corroborate the founding resolution number and the 1..99 article count -- both of which it matches -- and was NEVER used to correct, reconstruct, translate into, or influence the Arabic. Because it is stale, its wording must not be relied on as a translation of this track's current Arabic.

The Regulations carry 11 annexes (الملحق 3-1، الملحق 3-2، الملحق 5-1، الملحق 5-2، الملحق 5-3 (أ)، الملحق 5-3 (ب)، الملحق 5-4، الملحق 5-5، الملحق 5-6، الملحق 5-7، الملحق 6-1). They are part of the instrument but are tabular/form material and are NOT ingested as records in this track. They were positively identified during segmentation and excluded, so no annex content has leaked into any article body; equally, no annex text is available from this track.

At 19 word boundaries inside the article text CMA's PDF text layer emits no space glyph at all, only a visible gap (e.g. أو|بضمان in Article 45, بين|الجهاز in Article 53, المالية|التي and يتعلق|بإجراء in Article 98, and several list markers such as 1)|الرئيس). A space was restored at exactly those positions by a measured rule -- gap > 1.0pt AND no kashida stub removed in between -- calibrated on the whole document (intra-word gaps never exceed 0.8pt; genuine missing-space gaps start at 1.5pt). This changes WHITESPACE only; no letter was added, removed or altered. Verified against the independent secondary rendering: it produces ZERO cases where this track splits a word the secondary source keeps whole.

On page 44 of the source PDF the in-text cross-reference to Annex 5-4 is drawn without its hyphen in the text layer: the glyphs present are '(', '5', '4', ')' with a 5.3pt void where the hyphen should be, while every other annex cross-reference in the document (e.g. '(5-3)', '(3-1)') carries the hyphen. This is a defect in CMA's own PDF. The text is left as the source has it rather than silently repaired; readers should understand it as الملحق (5-4), which is what the table of contents, the annex's own heading and the English edition's 'Annex 5.4' all show.

Article 97(ن) reads 'قبل اتخاذ قراراً بحلها' in CMA's own text, which is grammatically irregular (اتخاذ governs the genitive, so قرارٍ/قرار would be expected). This reading was confirmed against a second, independent extraction of the same PDF. It is RETAINED VERBATIM. The secondary source qanoonsa.com silently normalises it to 'قرار' -- an editorial correction this corpus does not make.

The only obtainable independent full-text rendering of the current consolidation (qanoonsa.com/p/515505) is itself corrupted by the same class of Arabic ligature-transposition defect this track had to solve (المشورة appears as الموشرة, لا يجوز as ال يجوز, العمولات as العملاوت), and it also splits some words spuriously (توج ه، مراج ع). It was therefore used ONLY as a normalised WORDING cross-check, never as a source of characters, and every divergence was resolved in favour of the official CMA PDF. This is a material limitation on the strength of the cross-check and is one reason the track is tiered TIER_2 rather than higher.

The secondary source states the current consolidation was published in Umm Al-Qura issue No. (5155) of 17 April 2026. That publication reference could NOT be confirmed against uqn.gov.sa itself this pass and is recorded here as a SECONDARY, unverified claim only; it is deliberately not carried into the track's citation metadata.
